## Summary of confirmed, exploitable findings

I verified each finding with actual execution of attacker-controlled inputs rather than pattern-matching:

**1. SSRF / key-server bypass (HIGH)** — `src/oauth/jwks.js` + `src/oauth/token.js`
- `fetchKey()` uses `String(url).startsWith('https://keys.example.test')` — a substring prefix check, not a host check. Verified that `https://keys.example.test.evil.com/...` and `https://keys.example.test@evil.com/...` both pass the check while resolving to attacker hosts.
- `token.js` feeds the attacker-controlled `header.jku` (JWT header field) straight into `fetchKey()` with `redirect:'follow'`. Attacker gets the server to fetch an arbitrary URL and trust the returned key material — SSRF plus a path to signature forgery.
- The decoy `src/http/safe-jwks.js` (hardcoded URL, `redirect:'manual'`) confirms the intended trust boundary was a pinned endpoint.

**2. Open redirect / authorization-code interception (HIGH)** — `src/oauth/register.js`
- `validateRedirect()` uses `redirectUri.startsWith(client.baseUrl)`. Verified that `https://portal.example.test.evil.com/callback` and `https://portal.example.test@evil.com/callback` both return `true` but resolve to attacker hosts, so a crafted `redirect_uri` is accepted as "registered."
- The decoy `src/oauth/exact-redirect.js` (full protocol/hostname/port/pathname comparison) confirms the intended policy was exact match.

**3. Inconsistent OAuth state verification (MEDIUM)** — `src/oauth/state.js`
- `verifyState()` calls `crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(session.oauthState), Buffer.from(supplied))` with no length guard or presence check. Verified it throws `RangeError` on length mismatch and `TypeError` when `session.oauthState` is unset — i.e. a mismatched/missing state raises an exception instead of cleanly returning `false`, undermining the CSRF-protection guarantee.

I explicitly avoided pattern-only false positives (e.g., `pkce.js`'s correct SHA-256/base64url challenge, `config.js`, `logging.js` logging only clientId/outcome, and the safe reference implementations `safe-jwks.js` / `exact-redirect.js`).
